This is the restricted documentation for Creating, Retrieving, and Updating SkySlope Listings and Sales.

## FAQ

### Who do I contact for help?
The best resource for help is the SkySlope Support team. They can be reached at 1-800-507-4117 or by visiting support.skyslope.com to connect via chat.

### How can I get help authenticating?
The Authentication section of this documentation provides instructions on how to authenticate as well as some code examples for generating an HMAC. For an authentication example with video walkthrough please check out [this code repository](https://github.com/skyslope/example-authentication) and [video](https://www.loom.com/share/090cc16fb21b47688d97a35b99465489). If you need additional assistance authenticating, please reach out to the SkySlope Support Team.

### Where do I get the Client Id and Secret?
Your Customer Success Manager will assist with providing the Client Id and Secret in a password protected zip file. The password to access the zip file will be shared separately with your primary technical contact.

### Where do I get the access key and secret for a user?
The Access Key and Secret must be generated by each user from within their own SkySlope account. Detailed instructions on how to generate an Access Key and Secret are provided in the Getting started section of this documentation.

### Do I need to get each agent's authentication?
Yes for security reasons and compliance of the audit log, each user has their own Access Key and Secret they need to provide to integrate.

### As a vendor, do I need to get access from each brokerage?
Yes. You are required to get access from each brokerage.

### What do I have to do if I want to access multiple brokerages?
You will need to get the Access Key and Secret of each user from each brokerage that you wish to work with.

### How can I generate test data in my SkySlope test account to be used with the API?
When your test account is provided, it will not have any Listings or Sales populated. You can manually create property files from within the account or you can utilize the file creation scripts provided [here](https://github.com/skyslope/create-sample-files) to generate some test files.

### Do we have access to pull all fields?
Yes, you can pull all fields of the user you are integrated with using the Bulk Export endpoint. For an example of how to use the Bulk Export with video walkthrough please check out [this code repository](https://github.com/skyslope/bulk-export-api) and [video](https://www.loom.com/share/2b4276e52fa7464698bcae0b77b6be47) 

### Are we able to only pull certain fields?
Yes, our GraphQl endpoint can return the same data as the Bulk Export but if you do not need all of the data then you can specify which fields will come back in your response. More information for GraphQl can be found [here](https://github.com/skyslope/graphql-bulk-export-api) with a video tutorial [here](https://www.loom.com/share/c63eda77fe3348bb8eb70f3c323d14f7).

### What are your rate limits?
By default each Client Id is limited to 100 requests per minute. If you run into issues hitting the limit, you can utilize the rate limit headers returned in each response to know when to wait. More information about this in the Rate limiting section of this documentation.

### Do you offer webhooks? 
No, we do not offer webhooks.

### Where can I get a swagger or OpenAPI definition for SkySlope API?
You can download our [Swagger.json](swagger.json).

### How can I tell if the SkySlope API is down?
`GET /api/healthcheck` will return a  `200 OK` if everything is ok.

## 🔒 HMAC Authentication Process

### Authentication Overview
SkySlope uses HMAC-SHA256 authentication with the following process:

1. **POST** to `https://api.skyslope.com/auth/login`
2. **Include** required headers and payload
3. **Receive** session token (valid for 2 hours)
4. **Use** session token for all subsequent API calls

### Required Headers
```http
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: SS <AccessKey>:<HMAC>
Timestamp: <RFC3339_UTC_Timestamp>
```

### Request Payload
```json
{
  "clientID": "your_client_id",
  "clientSecret": "your_client_secret"
}
```

### HMAC Generation
The HMAC is computed using your `AccessSecret` as the key and this input:
```
<ClientID>:<ClientSecret>:<Timestamp>
```

### C# Authentication Example
```csharp
string clientId = "your_client_id";
string clientSecret = "your_client_secret"; 
string accessKey = "YOUR_ACCESS_KEY";
string accessSecret = "YOUR_ACCESS_SECRET";
string timestamp = DateTime.UtcNow.ToString("yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ");

var key = Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(accessSecret);
var input = $"{clientId}:{clientSecret}:{timestamp}";
var hmacBytes = new HMACSHA256(key).ComputeHash(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(input));
var hmac = Convert.ToBase64String(hmacBytes);
var authHeader = "SS " + accessKey + ":" + hmac;
```

### Node.js Authentication Example
```javascript
const crypto = require('crypto');
const clientId = "your_client_id";
const clientSecret = "your_client_secret";
const accessKey = "YOUR_ACCESS_KEY";
const accessSecret = "YOUR_ACCESS_SECRET";
const timestamp = new Date().toISOString();

const hmac = crypto.createHmac("sha256", accessSecret)
  .update(clientId + ":" + clientSecret + ":" + timestamp)
  .digest("base64");
const authHeader = "SS " + accessKey + ":" + hmac;
```

### Bash Authentication Example
```bash
TIMESTAMP=$(date -u "+%Y-%m-%dT%TZ")
HMAC=$(echo -n "$CLIENT_ID:$CLIENT_SECRET:$TIMESTAMP" | openssl sha256 -binary -hmac "$ACCESS_SECRET" | base64)

curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: SS $ACCESS_KEY:$HMAC" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Timestamp: $TIMESTAMP" \
  --data "{\\"ClientId\\":\\"$CLIENT_ID\\",\\"ClientSecret\\":\\"$CLIENT_SECRET\\"}" \
  https://api.skyslope.com/auth/login
```

### Authentication Response
```json
{
  "Session": "fe17fd08cf9fc17b7440d35b9b6d5d4429a2089f08b8b3f1faddcc5e56490920",
  "Expiration": "2019-07-11T20:34:50Z"
}
```

**Important Notes**:
- ⏰ **Timestamp Validity**: Must be within 5 minutes of UTC time
- 🕐 **Session Duration**: Sessions expire after 2 hours
- 🔄 **Token Renewal**: Get a new session by re-authenticating

## 📊 Rate Limits & Usage

### What are your rate limits?
- **Default Limit**: 100 requests per minute per Client ID
- **Monitoring**: Check rate limit headers in each response
- **Management**: Use headers to know when to wait before next request

### Rate Limit Headers
```http
x-ratelimit-limit: 100        # Total requests allowed per window
x-ratelimit-remaining: 85     # Requests remaining in current window  
x-ratelimit-reset: 1614290760 # When the next window starts (Unix timestamp)
```

### Example: Handling Rate Limits
```javascript
// Convert Unix timestamp to readable date
const resetTime = new Date(1614290760 * 1000).toISOString();
// Result: "2021-02-25T22:06:00.000Z"
```

get.description:
Overview

Retrieves the complete audit trail for a listing, showing all activities, changes, and events that have occurred throughout its lifecycle.

Audit Log Information

Each audit log entry includes:

  • Timestamp: When the activity occurred (ISO 8601 format with timezone)
  • Activity Type: The type of action performed (e.g., 'Document Uploaded', 'Status Changed')
  • Description: Detailed description of what happened (may include HTML formatting)
  • User: Name of the user who performed the action
  • Support User: If action was performed by support staff on behalf of user

Common Activity Types

  • Document uploads and removals
  • Status changes (Active, Pending, Sold, etc.)
  • Contact modifications (seller, agent changes)
  • Commission updates
  • Property detail changes
  • MLS synchronization events

  • Use startDate and endDate to filter by date range
  • Results are ordered by activity time (most recent first)
  • All matching audit logs are returned in a single response (consistent with existing SkySlope Prime behavior)

get.description:
Overview

Retrieves the complete audit trail for a sale, showing all activities, changes, and events that have occurred throughout its lifecycle.

Audit Log Information

Each audit log entry includes:

  • Timestamp: When the activity occurred (ISO 8601 format with timezone)
  • Activity Type: The type of action performed (e.g., 'Document Uploaded', 'Status Changed')
  • Description: Detailed description of what happened (may include HTML formatting)
  • User: Name of the user who performed the action
  • Support User: If action was performed by support staff on behalf of user

Common Activity Types

  • Document uploads and removals
  • Status changes (Pre-contract, Under Contract, Pending, Closed, etc.)
  • Contact modifications (buyer, seller, agent changes)
  • Commission updates and splits
  • Property detail changes
  • Earnest money deposit tracking
  • Conversion from pre-contract to under contract

    • Filtering

  • Use startDate and endDate to filter by date range
  • Results are ordered by activity time (most recent first)
  • All matching audit logs are returned in a single response (consistent with existing SkySlope Prime behavior)

    • Authorization

  • User must have access to the sale to view its audit logs
  • Audit logs are filtered by subscriber to ensure data isolation

tags.name: Bulk Export
tags.description:
## Overview

The Bulk Export endpoint provides high-performance streaming access to all sales and listings data. Unlike standard endpoints that return paginated results, this endpoint streams items to the response as they are retrieved from the database, allowing you to process large datasets efficiently without memory constraints.

## Response Format

The response is a standard JSON object with a `value` array:
```json
{"value": [<summary>, <listing>, ..., <sale>, ...], "links": [...]}
```
- Items inside the `value` array are flushed individually, separated by comma + newline
- You can begin processing items as they arrive without waiting for the full response
- The complete response is valid JSON once fully received

## Object Types

The response contains three types of objects, identifiable by the `objectType` field:

1. **summary** - First object in the stream, contains metadata about the export
2. **listing** - Represents a property listing with seller information
3. **sale** - Represents a transaction (buyer or seller side)

See the response schema for detailed field descriptions for each object type.

## Usage Examples

### Get Recent Modifications
```
GET /api/files?modifiedAfter=2024-01-01T08:00:00
```

### Get Incomplete Sales Only
```
GET /api/files?createdAfter=2000-01-01&status=incomplete&type=sale
```

### Get Active Listings in California
```
GET /api/files?status=active&type=listing&state=CA
```

### Filter by Date Range
```
GET /api/files?createdAfter=2024-01-01&createdBefore=2024-03-31
```

## Important Notes

- **Default Behavior**: Without date filters, returns files created within the last 7 days
- **Performance**: This endpoint is optimized for bulk data export and reporting
- **Streaming**: Items in the `value` array are flushed as they are retrieved — you can begin processing before the full response completes
- **Memory Efficient**: Process items from the `value` array incrementally to handle large datasets

## Available Statuses

| Status | Applies To | Description |
|--------|------------|-------------|
| **active** | listing | Current date is before expiration date |
| **archived** | sale | Closed and archived by auditor |
| **canceledApproved** | both | Cancellation has been approved |
| **canceledPending** | both | Submitted for cancellation approval |
| **closed** | sale | Closed by auditor |
| **expired** | both | Past expiration or closing date |
| **incomplete** | both | Missing required information |
| **pending** | sale | Current date is before closing date |

## Use Cases

- **Reporting**: Generate comprehensive reports across all transactions
- **Data Synchronization**: Keep external systems in sync with SkySlope data
- **Bulk Analysis**: Analyze trends across large datasets
- **Backup/Archive**: Export data for backup or compliance purposes

tags.name: Listings
tags.description:
## Overview
A Listing represents a property being sold by the owner (seller side), before entering into contract with a buyer. Listings are the foundation of real estate transactions in SkySlope.

## Key Concepts
- **Listing Lifecycle**: Created -> Active -> (Pending) -> Sold/Expired/Canceled
- **Required Fields**: Use `/api/files/listingForm` to get current requirements (fields are configurable per brokerage)
- **MLS Integration**: Listings can be synchronized with MLS systems
- **Document Management**: Each listing can have multiple documents attached
- **Agent Relationships**: Support for listing agents, co-agents, and referring agents

## Common Workflows

### Creating a New Listing
1. `GET /api/files/listingForm` - Get required fields and validation rules
2. `POST /api/files/listings` - Create the listing with seller information
3. `POST /api/files/listings/{id}/property` - Add property details
4. `POST /api/files/listings/{id}/sellerContact` - Add seller contacts
5. `POST /api/files/listings/{id}/documents` - Upload listing agreement and disclosures

### Managing Listing Status
- Active: Listing is currently on the market
- Pending: Under contract with a buyer
- Expired: Past the expiration date
- Canceled: Terminated before expiration
- Sold: Successfully closed

## Pagination

Results are returned in pages of 10 items by default. Use the PageNumber parameter to navigate:

    GET /api/files/listings?PageNumber=3  # Get items 21-30

The response includes HATEOAS links for navigation with href, rel, and method properties.

## Filtering

Filter listings using these parameters:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| earliestDate | long | Unix timestamp for start date |
| latestDate | long | Unix timestamp for end date |
| agentGuid | GUID | Filter by assigned agent |
| createdByGuid | GUID | Filter by creating user |

### Examples

**Get March 2024 listings for specific agent:**

    GET /api/files/listings?earliestDate=1709251200&latestDate=1711929599&agentGuid=123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000

**Get page 4 of listings created by specific user:**

    GET /api/files/listings?PageNumber=4&createdByGuid=987e6543-e21b-12d3-a456-426614174000

## Performance Tips
- Results are cached for 5 minutes
- Use date filters to limit result sets
- For bulk operations, use the Bulk Export endpoint
- Maximum 100 items per page

## Related Endpoints
- `/api/files/listings/{id}/property` - Property details
- `/api/files/listings/{id}/contacts/*` - Manage contacts
- `/api/files/listings/{id}/documents` - Document management
- `/api/files/listings/{id}/commissions` - Commission configuration

## Overview
A Sale represents a real estate transaction that is under contract or completed. Sales can represent either buyer-side or seller-side transactions, or both sides in a double-ended deal.

## Key Concepts
- **Sale Types**: Buyer Side, Seller Side, or Both Sides (double-ended)
- **Sale Lifecycle**: Pre-contract -> Under Contract -> Pending -> Closed -> Archived
- **Required Fields**: Use `/api/files/saleForm` to get current requirements (configurable per brokerage)
- **Conversion**: Pre-contract sales can be converted to under-contract when offer is accepted
- **Commission Tracking**: Comprehensive commission splits and calculations

## Common Workflows

### Creating a New Sale
1. `GET /api/files/saleForm` - Get required fields and validation rules
2. `POST /api/files/sales` - Create the sale with transaction details
3. `POST /api/files/sales/{id}/property` - Add property information
4. `POST /api/files/sales/{id}/buyerContact` - Add buyer contacts
5. `POST /api/files/sales/{id}/documents` - Upload purchase agreement and disclosures

### Converting Pre-Contract to Under Contract
1. `PUT /api/files/sales/{id}/convert/under-contract` - Convert when offer accepted
2. System updates status and triggers workflow changes
3. Additional checklist items become available

### Managing Sale Status
- **Pre-contract**: Offer stage, not yet accepted
- **Under Contract**: Accepted offer, working toward closing
- **Pending**: All contingencies removed, awaiting closing
- **Closed**: Transaction completed
- **Archived**: Closed and audited by compliance
- **Canceled**: Transaction terminated

## Pagination

Results are returned in pages of 10 items by default. Use the PageNumber parameter to navigate:

    GET /api/files/sales?PageNumber=3  # Get items 21-30

The response includes HATEOAS links for navigation with href, rel, and method properties.

## Filtering

Filter sales using these parameters:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| earliestDate | long | Unix timestamp for start date |
| latestDate | long | Unix timestamp for end date |
| agentGuid | GUID | Filter by assigned agent |
| createdByGuid | GUID | Filter by creating user |

### Examples

**Get March 2024 sales for specific agent:**

    GET /api/files/sales?earliestDate=1709251200&latestDate=1711929599&agentGuid=123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000

**Get page 4 of sales created by specific user:**

    GET /api/files/sales?PageNumber=4&createdByGuid=987e6543-e21b-12d3-a456-426614174000

## Commission Management
- Support for complex split arrangements
- Referral fee tracking
- Commission change audit log
- Integration with accounting systems

## Performance Tips
- Results are cached for 5 minutes
- Use date filters to limit result sets
- For bulk operations, use the Bulk Export endpoint
- Maximum 100 items per page

## Related Endpoints
- `/api/files/sales/{id}/property` - Property details
- `/api/files/sales/{id}/contacts/*` - Manage all parties
- `/api/files/sales/{id}/documents` - Document management
- `/api/files/sales/{id}/commissions` - Commission configuration
- `/api/files/sales/{id}/earnestMoney` - EMD tracking
